messages.author: 8e0ab9354e46fd5e
messages.subject: Trouble converting gl2gds
parts:
Hi all,

New dartR user here - I've recently received my data from Diversity Arrays and am trying to convert it from a genlight object to gds for further analysis. I keep getting the following error:

> Lepgds <- gl2gds(Lepdatanests, outfile = "gl2gds.gds", outpath = tempdir())
The SNP positions are not in ascending order on chromosome 1.

Any tips on how to solve this would be greatly appreciated!

Thank you!

messages.author: b3d929c6746ca81a
messages.subject: RE: [dartR] Trouble converting gl2gds
parts:
Maybe try to “delete” the position information from the genlight object (as it is not really meaningful as it is the number where the snp is on your 69 sequence and not the position on the chromosome).

 

 

Lepdatanests@position <- NULL

 

And the the

 

gl2gds

 

I have not played much with the gds function. You could also use the radiator package to convert to gds.

 

Cheers, Bernd

messages.author: 26c7c77e326f196c
messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Trouble converting gl2gds
parts:
Hi Isabelle,
You should be able to still use the .gds, even though it gives you the first error
The SNP positions are not in ascending order on chromosome 1.

This error does not effect the workflow.
The .gds should still be saved and usable in your tempdir. 

Since removing the position information gives you another error, I would recommend instead using the whole data set (with the position information) and try:

1. Setting a working directory and saving your output to there instead
2. then opening the .gds with the SNPRelate pkg.

This has always worked for me. I have attached the relevant code in case you want to try it.

Deane.

messages.subject: Re: [dartR] Trouble converting gl2gds
parts:
Is that error in response to the gl2gds() command?
Could you please run:

sessionInfo()

and post the output?

That error could be quite deep in the function. My recommendation (as always) would be to restart R, load packages again, and go though your script step by step. 
I think the problem might be in the adegenet package, which probably produces the "SNPbin", but I can't be sure without more context, and probably a lot more time.
Sorry.


Deane.

Sorry, I haven't had a chance to run a test for you.

If you want to try updating SNPRelate to 1.20.1 and downgrading adegenet to 2.1.1 (2.1.2 has been having several issues with genlights), there's a chance this could fix the problem.
If that doesn't work, I'll run a test using your specs.

Deane

install.packages("devtools")
library(devtools)
install_version("adegenet", version = "2.1.1", repos = "http://cran.us.r-project.org")
